claims.text: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio lists qwen3-max-2026-01-23 for international availability on January 27, describing merged thinking/non-thinking modes and built-in web search, web extraction, and code interpreter use during thinking.
The same lifecycle page records broad January 4 global availability for multiple Qwen3 and Wan 2.6 model families, including tool-oriented/coding and multimodal models.
Comparative capability language in the lifecycle catalog is vendor-reported and not independently reproduced.

claims.text: Z.ai release notes record GLM-Image on January 14, described as combining autoregressive semantic understanding with diffusion-based decoding for controllable image generation.
Z.ai release notes record GLM-4.7-Flash on January 19 as a lightweight/free-tier GLM-4.7 variant for coding, reasoning, and generative tasks.
Comparative quality, latency, throughput, and ‘best-in-class’ language in the release notes are vendor claims.

limitations.text: The task groups two distinct model releases because both establish the January Z.ai model line; drafting should not imply a single architecture.

claims.text: SGLang v0.5.8 added day-zero GLM-4.7-Flash support, expanded diffusion serving, FlashAttention 4 decoding support, and multiple long-context / disaggregated-serving changes.
Release-note performance figures such as up to 1.5x diffusion speedups, near-linear chunked-pipeline scaling, and a 65% TTFT improvement for a GLM4-MoE setup are project-reported claims.

limitations.text: The release aggregates many upstream PRs and performance claims across different models/hardware.
Model support establishes implementation availability, not equivalent quality or production validation.
